item.title: Raiders Issued Strong Fernando Mendoza Take Amid Three-Game Losing Skid
item.description: (Photo By Winslow Townson/Getty Images) Getty After a 3-0 start, the Las Vegas Raiders have dropped three straight games, with the latest loss coming to the Buffalo Bills in Week 6. Moreover, in Week 5, head coach Klint Kubiak decided to give Fernando Mendoza his regular-season debut in the loss to the New England Patriots. Amid the Raiders’ losing streak, the conversation is now about whether the team should start the Mendoza era. Nonetheless, former NFL QB Kurt Warner believes that now is not the right time for Las Vegas to turn to the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft and have him start over Kirk Cousins. “In my opinion, I don’t think they should as of yet,” Warner said during an Oct. 20 appearance on “The Rich Eisen Show.” “Again, I believe this team is not a great football team, but they’ve got some key pieces, including Kirk Cousins, that are making them competitive every time out. “I just think it’s too early right now, with how competitive and how well Kirk is playing, to go to Fernando just yet. It may come a time when you feel like this team is not good enough and not going to make a playoff push, and you make that move.” Raiders Would Send Wrong Message Turning to Fernando Mendoza Warner also believes that going with Mendoza right now would send the wrong message to the veteran players on the team that are wanting to compete, as the Raiders are at .500 and could move to 4-3 if they can get a win over the struggling Los Angeles Rams in Week 6. “I just don’t think the time is right now,” Warner added. “I think Kirk gives them confidence right now that, ‘Hey, even if we’re not winning these games, we’re competitive every single time out,’ which I think is really important for that organization right now, for guys like Maxx Crosby and for a first-time head coach. “It’s really important to be competitive every single time out and until that season kind of moves from that mode to ‘ Okay , probably not going to be in the playoffs,’ I think you stay with Kirk as long as he’s playing good football.” Kirk Cousins’ Play Should Determine Any QB Change Meanwhile, for CBS Sports’ Pete Prisco, he sees the situation playing out with Cousins’ play being the sole factor. Cousins has performed well, and the Raiders have won games, but once that stops, Prisco believes it’s time for Mendoza. “ Kirk Cousins has earned the right to stay in there,” Prisco said during an Oct. 11 appearance on “CBS Sports HQ.” “As long as you’re winning football games, or at least competing in games for the next couple of weeks, he’ll stay in there. But if he has a couple of bad games, then I think it becomes Fernando Mendoza time. “I’m a big believer that the sooner you get to the guy, the better off it is for the organization. As long as they’re competing and staying in games, the next two weeks are going to be tough. They have a brutal schedule over the next two weeks. item.title: Brewers World Series costs: How high have prices soared since 1982?
item.description: Things have changed since the last time the Milwaukee Brewers played in a World Series. In 1982, when the Brewers ultimately lost to the St. Louis Cardinals in their first World Series, the cost of a hot dog at County Stadium was $1.10. A 16-ounce beer cost $1.60 – and if you could track down an aisle vendor, a 12-ounce beer would go for $1.40. Now, a junior hot dog at American Family Field will cost you $4 and a domestic beer could set you back about $13 at most of the draft bars in the stadium. A stadium representative told the Journal Sentinel beer prices vary depending on brand and size, but a standard Miller Lite comes out to $13.24. But if you're thinking those older prices are outrageously low, take a look at a column by Mike Kupper published in The Milwaukee Journal on July 8, 1982. "No, I don't think you could really call it a bargain," Kupper wrote. "It's no more expensive than many other family entertainments, but it's not cheap, either, unless you're willing to put up with the no-frills, bare-bones approach. And I ask you: What would baseball be without a beer or a hot dog?" Here's the concessions prices Kupper reported in 1982 and how they compare to current prices. Concession 1982 Price 2026 Price Hot dog $1.10 $4.00 Bratwurst $1.30 $8.00 Soda (medium) $0.90 $4.00 Beer $1.60 (16 oz. draft) $13.24 Popcorn $1.75 $4.00 Nachos $1.40 $4.00 Peanuts $0.80 $4.00 Lots of historic baseball staple snacks end up on the stadium's 414 Menu, an updated concession menu that cut many snacks down to $4 in 2023. The rising concession prices have outpaced inflation over the years. If you only adjusted for inflation, a $1.10 hot dog in July 1982 would cost $3.80 in 2026, while that $1.60 beer would be about $5.53, according to the Consumer Price Index calculator . But concessions might feel like a steal compared to tickets. Most tickets to the 1982 World Series cost between $8 and $18, according to multiple news outlets and Brewers fans on social media . Tickets to Game 1 of the 2026 World Series in Milwaukee are selling for $2,700 or more. But other than tickets, one of the most sizeable increases shows up in the cost of parking. "It costs $3 these days to park in the stadium lot, which is excessive, considering that normally there still is a healthy walk involved after parking," Kupper reported in 1982. On a regular game day in 2026, parking at American Family Field costs $44. And, according to StubHub, parking passes for the 2026 World Series start at $119. More: See where drinks, hot dogs are cheapest at stadiums across league Other non-stadium costs have gone up since 1982 A gallon of gas in the Midwest was just $1.29 cents on average in July 1982, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. On Oct. 20, 2026, the average gallon of gas in Wisconsin cost $4.18. Minimum wage in Wisconsin was $3.25 an hour, and $1.95 an hour for tipped employees, in 1982. item.title: Butch Harmon urges the PGA Tour to make big change in the absence of Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Butch Harmon has been around the very highest level of the game for more than six decades now. Harmon has coached some of the greatest golfers ever to have graced the game, including Tiger Woods, Phil Mickelson and Greg Norman. The 83-year-old is one of the most knowledgeable people in the game, and everything he says always carries real weight. Butch Harmon obviously knows Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson inside out, but he is also a keen follower of emerging talents coming through the ranks on the PGA Tour . And Harmon has highlighted one thing he believes the PGA Tour needs to do much more of regarding their promotion of the supremely talented batch of youngsters coming through. Butch Harmon urges PGA Tour to make changes in the absence of Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson While speaking on the No Laying Up Podcast, Harmon was asked to give his opinion on the current state of the game. “ I think we have the best crop of young players we’ve ever had, “ Harmon suggested. They’re unbelievable. That’s the plus side. The downside for TV is that nobody knows who these players are. “ They’ll turn on the TV, and if some of the stars aren’t up there, and they see these guys 20, 23, under, they go, I don’t know who that is, and they change the channel. “ So I don’t think the PGA Tour does a good enough job of promoting the younger players through special stuff where you can learn about their lives and stuff. “ If you look at young players on the PGA Tour, the DP World Tour, the Asian Tour, they’re unbelievable these kids. There are a lot of them, and there are more of them coming. “ So the game is changing completely to what it used to be because the big stars are not there anymore. Tiger’s gone, Phil’s gone. All the other guys are gone. You know, all the ones you grew up with are all on the Champions Tour now. “ Harmon makes a great point. There are so many incredibly talented young players coming through the ranks on the PGA Tour right now. And the tour really needs to make more of an effort to showcase them. Perhaps a series on The Golf Channel examining the personalities of these players and giving fans a behind the scenes look at their lives would do the trick. This would enable golf fans to forge more of a connection with the young stars of the modern era and perhaps then the likes of Michael Brennan, Jackson Koivun and co. would become the next true superstars of the game.

Butch Harmon urges PGA Tour to make changes in the absence of Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson While speaking on the No Laying Up Podcast, Harmon was asked to give his opinion on the current state of the game. “ I think we have the best crop of young players we’ve ever had, “ Harmon suggested. They’re unbelievable. That’s the plus side. The downside for TV is that nobody knows who these players are. “ They’ll turn on the TV, and if some of the stars aren’t up there, and they see these guys 20, 23, under, they go, I don’t know who that is, and they change the channel. “ So I don’t think the PGA Tour does a good enough job of promoting the younger players through special stuff where you can learn about their lives and stuff. “ If you look at young players on the PGA Tour, the DP World Tour, the Asian Tour, they’re unbelievable these kids. There are a lot of them, and there are more of them coming. “ So the game is changing completely to what it used to be because the big stars are not there anymore. Tiger’s gone, Phil’s gone. All the other guys are gone. You know, all the ones you grew up with are all on the Champions Tour now. “ Harmon makes a great point. There are so many incredibly talented young players coming through the ranks on the PGA Tour right now. And the tour really needs to make more of an effort to showcase them. Perhaps a series on The Golf Channel examining the personalities of these players and giving fans a behind the scenes look at their lives would do the trick. This would enable golf fans to forge more of a connection with the young stars of the modern era and perhaps then the likes of Michael Brennan, Jackson Koivun and co. would become the next true superstars of the game.

item.title: Packers Trade Pitch Targets Colts’ 3-Time Pro Bowler for 4th-Round Pick
item.description: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 02: DeForest Buckner #99 of the Indianapolis Colts warms up against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the game at Acrisure Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) Getty The Green Bay Packers have already lost one veteran defensive tackle for the season. Now, a new trade proposal has them looking to the Indianapolis Colts for another established player who could help their defense down the stretch. DeForest Buckner has continued to produce in Indianapolis, but the Colts are 2-4, general manager Chris Ballard has been fired and the 32-year-old made his frustration clear following Sunday’s loss to the Tennessee Titans. With the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline approaching, Green Bay has been named as a potential landing spot for Buckner in a deal that wouldn’t require a premium draft pick. DeForest Buckner Trade Pitch Names Packers as Suitor Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox listed Buckner at No. 4 on his Oct. 21 trade block rankings, projecting a 2027 fourth-round pick as the price to acquire him. Knox named the Packers and San Francisco 49ers as potential suitors. The proposal followed the Colts’ decision to fire Ballard on Monday, one day after a 26-20 home loss to the previously winless Titans. Indianapolis named assistant GM Ed Dodds to oversee its personnel department for the remainder of the season. Knox suggested the leadership change could put veteran players on the market if ownership decides to shift its focus toward the future. “Premier defensive tackles generally command strong returns, and Buckner is still one of those, even at 32,” Knox wrote. Buckner has started all six games this season, totaling 26 tackles, four sacks and three passes defended. The three-time Pro Bowler is in the final year of his contract, which could make him a short-term addition for a team pursuing a playoff run. His comments following the loss to Tennessee have also attracted attention. “I’m sick and tired of the same song and dance every year,” Buckner said, via NFL.com’s Kevin Patra . Buckner also said he still had confidence in the people in Indianapolis when asked about the coaching staff and front office. His comments were about the Colts’ struggles, rather than a trade request. DeForest Buckner Could Address Packers’ Injury-Hit Defense Green Bay has a more immediate reason to consider the idea. Defensive tackle Javon Hargrave is out for the season with an Achilles injury. The Packers also placed Jonathan Ford on injured reserve before their Week 6 victory over the Dallas Cowboys . The team signed former first-round pick Mazi Smith to its practice squad Tuesday, but that move provides depth rather than the proven interior pass rush Buckner could offer alongside Devonte Wyatt. The team signed former first-round pick Mazi Smith to its practice squad Tuesday, but that move provides depth rather than the proven interior pass rush Buckner could offer alongside Devonte Wyatt. The Packers are 4-2 following their 23-13 win over Dallas, their third straight victory. Their defense intercepted Dak Prescott twice and held the Cowboys to 48 rushing yards. For the Packers, Knox’s suggested fourth-round price would offer a chance to add an experienced pass rusher without parting with an early selection. Indianapolis would have to decide whether getting that pick is worth losing one of its most productive defenders midway through another difficult season. item.title: Albany native, Green Tech grad U-Mier Graham ready to contribute immediately for UAlbany men's basketball
item.description: U-Mier Graham, who once starred at Green Tech, is expected to contribute as a freshman this season for the UAlbany men's basketball team. (Lori Van Buren/Times Union) ALBANY - Nagging injuries have made it tough for the University at Albany men's basketball team to consistently do 5-on-5 work this preseason. On one of those rare occasions last week when the Great Danes did get to do just that, though, one of the members playing among the presumed starting five was a bit surprising. Freshman forward U-Mier Graham, an Albany native and former Green Tech High standout, was part of UAlbany's first unit playing power forward. He was joined in the frontcourt by Erwann Bussing and Papa Kounta, with Ollie Engen and fellow Albany native Zacharie Matulu at the guard spots. There's no guarantee that the 6-foot-7 Graham will be in the starting lineup when UAlbany opens its season Nov. 2 against Rhode Island College, especially as fellow forwards Abdoulaye Fall and Pedro Santos make their way back from injury, but the freshman has been one of the players who has impressed UAlbany coach Dwayne Killings the most since arriving on campus. "He's played really well at the four and the five," Killings said. In high school, Graham was a Times Union all-star as both a junior and a senior, averaging double-digit points and rebounds in both campaigns. As a junior in 2024, he helped lead Green Tech to a Class AAA state championship, while his senior season ended with a Section 2 final loss to eventual state champion Shaker. Graham then spent a post-graduate year at The Knox School on Long Island playing under Jared Grasso, the former head coach at UAlbany's America East rival Bryant. That post-grad season helped Graham expand his on-court game, but it was his growth from being away from home that aided the forward most in his transition to college basketball. "It gave me a chance to learn how to be away from my family for a long time," he said. "I just knew that I could always look for my teammates - my brothers - and make sure that we're connected." Like Matulu, a Shaker High grad and UAlbany's top returning scorer, Graham said he's thrilled to be playing at home in front of local crowds, with friends and family easily able to attend the Great Danes' home games at Broadview Center. But, Graham said, he's also adamant in keeping his home life and his basketball life as separate entities to avoid distractions. "I'm glad to be back home, but it's good that I separate home from basketball, because I'm here to do a job," he said. "I'm here to work. That's the goal." item.title: Bayern Munich v Arsenal Preview: Team News, Predicted Lineup & Score Prediction
item.description: Bayern Munich v Arsenal Preview: Team News, Predicted Lineup & Score Prediction It’s matchday, Gooners! And what a Champions League night we have ahead of us! Arsenal are heading to the Allianz Arena to face Bayern Munich, with two European victories already under our belts and a formidable challenge awaiting in Germany. After a hard-fought 1-0 victory at Napoli and a convincing 3-0 win over Lille , Mikel Arteta’s side are chasing a remarkable 15th consecutive Champions League league-phase victory. But Bayern Munich at home? That’s another challenge entirely. Bayern’s fortress meets Arsenal’s European momentum Bayern have lost just once in their last 31 Champions League home matches, winning 24. That’s quite a record, although Arsenal have reason to approach tonight with confidence. Our 3-1 victory over Bayern at the Emirates last November remains the only occasion in their last 23 European matches that they’ve lost by more than one goal. And Arsenal’s away form in Europe is impressive too, unbeaten in eight Champions League away matches, with six victories and five clean sheets. Bayern are unbeaten in the Bundesliga this season and arrive fresh from a 6-1 victory over Leipzig. However, their recent 3-3 Champions League draw against Viking exposed defensive vulnerabilities. As Arsenal’s official match preview highlights, Bayern have managed just three clean sheets in their opening ten matches across competitions. There will be opportunities tonight. The question is whether we can take them! (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) Team news and the battle that could decide tonight There’s welcome news for Arsenal, with Martin Zubimendi available again after recovering from injury. Piero Hincapié remains unavailable, alongside William Saliba and Christos Tzolis. Bayern also have problems. Michael Olise is suspended , Jamal Musiala is injured, and Manuel Neuer remains a doubt. But Harry Kane will demand plenty of attention. His movement into midfield could cause problems for Arsenal’s defensive organisation, while Luis Díaz offers serious pace and attacking threat out wide. Arteta is clearly relishing the occasion. “I’m really looking forward to the game, this is the stage, this is the kind of team, this is the kind of coach, this is the kind of club, the stadium that you want to be involved in.” Predicted Lineup: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimarães, Rice; Saka, Ødegaard, Madueke; Gyökeres Score prediction: Bayern Munich 1-2 Arsenal COYG! So, Gooners, do you share Arteta’s enthusiasm? Can Arsenal silence the Allianz Arena and make it three Champions League victories from three? What’s your score prediction and predicted lineup tonight? item.title: Columns and Courts: Mizzou Tennis takeaways
item.description: Missouri women’s tennis has spent the opening months of its fall season adjusting to a new coaching staff, evaluating its roster and building chemistry as the Tigers prepare for the spring dual-match schedule. Head coach Robin Goodman, who was hired in May 2026, has used the fall tournaments to establish his expectations and learn more about a roster that features just one returning player from last season. Associate head coach Manny Raga and assistant coach Bronte Murgett have joined Goodman in helping guide the program through the transition. The fall schedule has provided an early opportunity for the staff to evaluate individual performances while emphasizing the importance of competing together, particularly as the team works toward its goals for the upcoming spring season. Building chemistry under a new staff The ITA Central Regional Championships marked an important checkpoint for Missouri, bringing together all three coaches and the Tigers’ nine player roster for the tournament. Missouri recorded 11 wins on the opening day of competition Thursday, Oct. 15, giving the team early momentum and opportunities to test itself against regional competition. Goodman was encouraged by the team’s willingness to compete and support one another throughout the tournament, pointing to those qualities as important parts of the program’s development. “Another great tournament for us,” Goodman said. “Really proud of the way these girls fight and their willingness to support one another.” The tournament also gave the coaching staff more time to assess how its players respond to competitive situations and work alongside their teammates. With a brand new group coming together, those experiences could prove valuable when Missouri transitions to the spring season, when dual matches will place a greater emphasis on collective results. A young roster gains valuable experience Missouri entered the fall with nine players, seven of whom are freshmen, alongside sophomore Alex Ackman and junior Millie Skelton, a transfer from SMU. Ackman is well documented as the only player returning from last season’s roster, making the early tournaments especially important for a team learning to compete under a new staff. The Tigers opened the fall at the Husker Invitational in September before traveling to Charlotte for the 49er Invite. Missouri earned 12 wins against opponents including Charlotte, Clemson, Maryland and Rutgers at the latter tournament, continuing a productive start to the season. The ITA Central Regional Championships provided another encouraging result, as Missouri finished with 17 wins across three days of competition. Ackman and freshman Daria Budko advanced in the singles main draw, while all four Missouri doubles teams won their opening matches to give the Tigers a 4-0 start in doubles play. item.content:encoded: Missouri women’s tennis has spent the opening months of its fall season adjusting to a new coaching staff, evaluating its roster and building chemistry as the Tigers prepare for the spring dual-match schedule. Head coach Robin Goodman, who was hired in May 2026, has used the fall tournaments to establish his expectations and learn more about a roster that features just one returning player from last season. Associate head coach Manny Raga and assistant coach Bronte Murgett have joined Goodman in helping guide the program through the transition. The fall schedule has provided an early opportunity for the staff to evaluate individual performances while emphasizing the importance of competing together, particularly as the team works toward its goals for the upcoming spring season. Building chemistry under a new staff The ITA Central Regional Championships marked an important checkpoint for Missouri, bringing together all three coaches and the Tigers’ nine player roster for the tournament. Missouri recorded 11 wins on the opening day of competition Thursday, Oct. 15, giving the team early momentum and opportunities to test itself against regional competition. Goodman was encouraged by the team’s willingness to compete and support one another throughout the tournament, pointing to those qualities as important parts of the program’s development. “Another great tournament for us,” Goodman said. “Really proud of the way these girls fight and their willingness to support one another.” The tournament also gave the coaching staff more time to assess how its players respond to competitive situations and work alongside their teammates. With a brand new group coming together, those experiences could prove valuable when Missouri transitions to the spring season, when dual matches will place a greater emphasis on collective results. A young roster gains valuable experience Missouri entered the fall with nine players, seven of whom are freshmen, alongside sophomore Alex Ackman and junior Millie Skelton, a transfer from SMU. Ackman is well documented as the only player returning from last season’s roster, making the early tournaments especially important for a team learning to compete under a new staff. The Tigers opened the fall at the Husker Invitational in September before traveling to Charlotte for the 49er Invite. Missouri earned 12 wins against opponents including Charlotte, Clemson, Maryland and Rutgers at the latter tournament, continuing a productive start to the season. The ITA Central Regional Championships provided another encouraging result, as Missouri finished with 17 wins across three days of competition. Ackman and freshman Daria Budko advanced in the singles main draw, while all four Missouri doubles teams won their opening matches to give the Tigers a 4-0 start in doubles play. The tournament also showed the challenges that come with competing against established programs. Ackman and freshman Danielle Chapman both played three-set matches in the main draw’s round of 32 but were unable to advance, providing experience in high-pressure situations that could benefit them later in the season. Looking ahead to the spring Missouri’s early results suggest the team is making progress, but the primary takeaway is the development happening beyond the win-loss column. Goodman and his staff are establishing expectations for consistency, discipline and communication while the players learn how to compete alongside one another. The Tigers will continue that process at the Jae Foundation Invite, hosted by TCU in Fort Worth, Texas, from Oct. 22-24. The tournament offers another opportunity for Missouri’s young roster to gain experience. With a new coaching staff and an almost entirely new roster, Missouri still has plenty to establish before the spring season begins. However, the Tigers’ steady collection of wins and growing team chemistry have given Goodman an encouraging starting point as he works to build the program’s future. Tiger Top Spin will be back next Monday recapping the Jae Foundation Invite. Columns and Courts will return next Wednesday looking forward to ITA sectionals.

item.title: Bears vs. Patriots: Can Grady Jarrett beat the ailing Pats interior?
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles scrambles from Grady Jarrett #50 of the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s a quick turnaround week, which always magnifies the injury report for teams. The Bears are not without injuries, as Kyle Monangai, Jonah Jackson, and TJ Edwards have all been sidelined this week. The Patriots, however, had their OL decimated on Sunday against the Jets. Guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown, and Tackle Morgan Moses all had varying injuries Sunday that put their statuses in question for Thursday’s matchup in Chicago. This adds to an already ailing OL in New England with Greg Van Roten, Michael Owenwu, and Marcus Bryant on IR. This leaves the Bears with a golden opportunity — get pressure up the middle, and disrupt Drake Maye quickly. The third year QB currently has his highest career pressure % at 26.2%, an uptick of 5% from last season. Losing three starters isn’t going to help. You have to expect a combination of rookie Caleb Lomu, Matt Pryor, and Walter Rouse to fill in for their teammates’ absences. Lomu and Rouse have about 300 snaps in their careers between them, while Pryor — a vet that Bears fans are very familiar with — has a fair amount of experience and is capable of providing quality starts. Still, this opens up a major opportunity for the Bears. Enter Grady Jarrett. Jarrett, one of the big DL acquisitions in the 2025 offseason, has been more disruptive in 2026 than 2025, despite his numbers still lagging. While he hasn’t yet recorded a sack, he has 5 pressures, 3 hurries, and two QB hits through 6 games this season. Much of his game needs to be seen live, though, as his presence has been felt more often, setting up others for sacks or impact plays. For instance, watch this sack Dayo Odeyingbo has on Jalen Hurts. Grady Jarrett’s stunt and pressure forces Hurts to step up, right into the arms of Dayo: Dayo Odeyingbo comes up BIG for the SACK on Jalen Hurts 😤 pic.twitter.com/XL4pIuvirJ — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) September 29, 2026 This is the type of impact Jarrett is going to have to make on Thursday against a jump start Patriots squad. After starting the season 1-2, New England is on a bit of a tear, winning their last three games by a combined 38 points. Maye is at the center of that, and he has proven to have a propensity for going downfield, as evidenced by his 5th-best 8.0 yards per pass attempt. The Packers game illustrated the Bears’ weakness in covering deep passes, and their need to maintain several defenders in coverage against QBs with a strong deep ball. So getting pressure on four man fronts will be even more critical for the Bears. With Grady Jarrett going up against two potential backups in Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse, he could do some serious damage in limiting Maye’s ability to throw downfield. item.content:encoded: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles scrambles from Grady Jarrett #50 of the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s a quick turnaround week, which always magnifies the injury report for teams. The Bears are not without injuries, as Kyle Monangai, Jonah Jackson, and TJ Edwards have all been sidelined this week. The Patriots, however, had their OL decimated on Sunday against the Jets. Guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown, and Tackle Morgan Moses all had varying injuries Sunday that put their statuses in question for Thursday’s matchup in Chicago. This adds to an already ailing OL in New England with Greg Van Roten, Michael Owenwu, and Marcus Bryant on IR. This leaves the Bears with a golden opportunity — get pressure up the middle, and disrupt Drake Maye quickly. The third year QB currently has his highest career pressure % at 26.2%, an uptick of 5% from last season. Losing three starters isn’t going to help. You have to expect a combination of rookie Caleb Lomu, Matt Pryor, and Walter Rouse to fill in for their teammates’ absences. Lomu and Rouse have about 300 snaps in their careers between them, while Pryor — a vet that Bears fans are very familiar with — has a fair amount of experience and is capable of providing quality starts. Still, this opens up a major opportunity for the Bears. Enter Grady Jarrett. Jarrett, one of the big DL acquisitions in the 2025 offseason, has been more disruptive in 2026 than 2025, despite his numbers still lagging. While he hasn’t yet recorded a sack, he has 5 pressures, 3 hurries, and two QB hits through 6 games this season. Much of his game needs to be seen live, though, as his presence has been felt more often, setting up others for sacks or impact plays. For instance, watch this sack Dayo Odeyingbo has on Jalen Hurts. Grady Jarrett’s stunt and pressure forces Hurts to step up, right into the arms of Dayo: Dayo Odeyingbo comes up BIG for the SACK on Jalen Hurts 😤 pic.twitter.com/XL4pIuvirJ — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) September 29, 2026 This is the type of impact Jarrett is going to have to make on Thursday against a jump start Patriots squad. After starting the season 1-2, New England is on a bit of a tear, winning their last three games by a combined 38 points. Maye is at the center of that, and he has proven to have a propensity for going downfield, as evidenced by his 5th-best 8.0 yards per pass attempt. The Packers game illustrated the Bears’ weakness in covering deep passes, and their need to maintain several defenders in coverage against QBs with a strong deep ball. So getting pressure on four man fronts will be even more critical for the Bears. With Grady Jarrett going up against two potential backups in Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse, he could do some serious damage in limiting Maye’s ability to throw downfield. If the Bears are to win this Thursday, I think that Jarrett needs to create one or two sacks for himself or others. If he doesn’t, it may force Allen to generate some blitzes and Maye could pick them apart.

item.title: Scottish FA confirm match officials for Celtic’s trip to Easter Road
item.description: Scottish FA confirm match officials for Celtic’s trip to Easter Road The Scottish FA have confirmed the match officials for Celtic’s Scottish Premiership encounter against Hibernian at Easter Road on Sunday. Referee Ryan Lee checks the VAR screen during the Scottish Premiership match between St. Mirren and Celtic at St Mirren Park on September 05, 2026. (Photo by Zak Mauger/Getty Images) Martin O’Neill’s side travel to Edinburgh looking to build on their emphatic 7-1 victory over Hearts last weekend, which provided a significant boost to confidence following a difficult period for the Scottish champions. The Hoops currently sit at the top of the Premiership table, while Hibernian find themselves rooted to the bottom following a disappointing start to the campaign. New Hibs manager Marink Reedijk has endured a difficult introduction to life at Easter Road, losing both of his opening matches in charge, including last weekend’s defeat to Falkirk. Ahead of Sunday’s meeting, the Scottish FA have now confirmed the refereeing team responsible for overseeing the encounter. Ryan Lee has been appointed as the match referee, with Chris Rae and Scott Anderson serving as his assistants. Iain Snedden will take up fourth official duties, while experienced referee Nick Walsh will oversee VAR operations, assisted by Duncan Williams. item.title: Confirmed Man United XI vs Como
item.description: Confirmed Man United XI vs Como Manchester United visit Como today for an early kick-off in the Champions League. Head coach Michael Carrick remains under intense pressure having failed to beat Leeds United on Sunday and has to deal with the absence of a host of first-team stars. Here is the confirmed line-up for the game. Goalkeeper and Defence Senne Lammens is in goal. Diogo Dalot is at right back. Harry Maguire continues at centre-back. More to follow … Leny Yoro is suspended. Luke Shaw, Lisandro Martinez and Patrick Dorgu are all injured and Ayden Heaven is unwell. Midfield Carlos Baleba retains his place in central midfield and is partnered again by Andrey Santos, with Youri Tielemans playing ahead of them. Kobbie Mainoo did not travel, and Manu Ugarte has a long-term injury. Attack Bruno Fernandes stays in a forward role, with Bryan Mbeumo retaining his place up front. Amad continues on the right side of midfield. Ben Sesko is out injured. Marcus Rashford is carrying a knock. Substitutes To follow. Final Thoughts Featured image by Jan Kruger via Getty Images online polls

item.title: How Arsenal could beat Juventus to prolific German star
item.description: How Arsenal could beat Juventus to prolific German star Nicolo Tresoldi has emerged as one of the most exciting young forwards in Europe, and his Champions League hat-trick against Inter Milan has increased Juventus’ interest in signing him . The Club Brugge striker is attracting attention after his impressive performances, with several clubs now considering a move for his signature. Juventus could regret not pursuing him more seriously during the summer transfer window. The Bianconeri concentrated much of their effort on bringing Randal Kolo Muani from Paris Saint-Germain and may have missed an opportunity to sign Tresoldi, who had already shown his quality last season. His continued development at Club Brugge has made him an increasingly attractive target. It is perhaps surprising that no major club secured his services during the previous transfer window, but his recent performances have ensured that interest is growing. Arsenal push to sign Tresoldi in January According to The Sun , Arsenal are keen to move for Tresoldi in January rather than wait until the end of the season. The Gunners are reportedly determined to strengthen their attacking options, and the striker has emerged as a potential target. Arsenal could also make changes to their forward line, with Viktor Gyokeres potentially leaving in a future transfer window. If that happens, signing Tresoldi could become an important part of their recruitment plans. However, securing the Club Brugge forward would require a significant financial commitment. Juventus are also interested, but they may be reluctant to spend the amount required to complete a January deal. That could give Arsenal an advantage in the race, particularly if they are prepared to meet Club Brugge’s demands during the winter window. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) Juventus could wait until the summer Juventus have not necessarily lost their opportunity to sign Tresoldi. If the striker remains at Club Brugge until the end of the season, the Bianconeri could revisit their interest after making sales and creating more room in their transfer budget. Waiting, however, would carry risks. Arsenal could secure an agreement in January, leaving Juventus to consider alternative targets if the forward moves to the Premier League. Tresoldi would also need to decide which destination best suits his ambitions. A move to England could appeal to him, but Juventus could still offer an attractive opportunity if they can put together a convincing proposal. For now, Arsenal’s reported willingness to act in January could prove decisive. Juventus may need to reconsider their financial approach if they want to compete for the striker’s signature.

item.title: Giants Trade Pitch Sends RB Cam Skattebo to Super Bowl Contender
item.description: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo. Getty It’s pretty obvious that New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh has reached the end of his rope with running back Cam Skattebo — a slow progression that started with an offseason of missteps and culminated in Harbaugh benching Skattebo in Week 6 after fumbles became an issue that cost his team wins. Skattebo will only have trade value for the Giants right now, and they need to move him by the November 10 trade deadline if they want any return on their investment. One team that might leap at giving up a Day 3 pick for Skattebo is the Super Bowl-contending Buffalo Bills, where Skattebo could be a great change-of-pace back alongside starter and NFL All-Pro James Cook — another player with fumbling issues. In this case, the Giants might expect a 6th- or 7th-round pick back — if not, they might cut Skattebo outright after the trade deadline. “The Giants would also love to alter things at running back, apparently,” ESPN’s Dan Graziano wrote on October 21 . “The new coaching staff has clearly soured on Cam Skattebo, the Giants just released Najee Harris, and it wouldn’t be shocking to see them add someone from the outside or give Tyrone Tracy Jr. a bigger chance.” Giants Benched Skattebo Against Saints The Giants benched Skattebo, their leading rusher, after a disastrous fumble cost them a Week 5 win against the Washington Commanders — a game that ended in a tie — and he didn’t get any carries in a Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints . When asked about benching Skattebo against the Saints — Harbaugh tried to pull off a Jedi mind trick. “We didn’t bench Cam Skattebo,” Harbaugh said. “That wasn’t by design … they were all pretty equal in the first half (with snaps). It wasn’t intentional that he didn’t carry the ball. You’re not thinking about what running back is in the game or how many carries they’re getting … we’re going to give them all equal shots. See who got a hot hand … you’re balancing it between four guys. Do the math.” Harbaugh Called Skattebo ‘Disease’ in Training Camp Harbaugh has been open about his disgust with Skattebo almost since he got the job with the Giants — a stretch that saw Skattebo at the heart of a controversy where he denied concussions and asthma were real things in the offseason as well as a failed backflip attempt during a Fanatics event on a surgically-repaired leg before training camp. During training camp, after one practice in which Skattebo began to draw the ire of his teammates after several bizarre stunts — including running over a linebacker during a non-contact practice — Harbaugh unloaded on him. “He got a 15-yard penalty at the end of practice,” Harbaugh said in August. “Did you see that? Yeah it’s infectious. It can be infectious the other way, an infectious disease type of thing. We want it to be in a positive way.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Giants Trade Pitch Sends RB Cam Skattebo to Super Bowl Contender appeared first on HEAVY

item.title: Como v Manchester United: Champions League – live
item.description: ⚽️ Champions League updates from 5.45pm BST ⚽️ Live scoreboard | Champions League table | Mail Simon Hello world! And welcome to this, a tale of two managers. Poor Michael Carrick, for all his undoubted ability, has been negatively compared for Cesc Fabregas for many years. Back in October 2009 the Guardian’s late, great football correspondent David Lacey wrote a column in praise of the Spaniard’s reliable brilliance – “Bergkamp did have off days, whereas Fabregas just has the odd day off” – in which Carrick was referred to, in passing, as a “gifted water carrier”. And here they are, 17 years and a few days later, up against each other once again, in a different role, one of them obviously good, the other evidently better. Transfermarkt estimates the value of Como’s squad at €568.15m, and Manchester United’s at €928.80m. Como have lost only once in the league this season, while United have won only once. Both have one win and one defeat in their first two Champions League fixtures. And tonight seems destined to be discussed primarily in terms of how it affects Carrick’s standing and chances of long-term employment. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Champions League drama galore – so why do we feel hollow?
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Now then, which one of you hipsters decided to put Porto 0-1 PSV on? Oh dear. This was another night of Bigger Cup at its Bigliest self, comebacks everywhere, 40 goals in nine games, six of those in a best-v-best clash as Paris Saint-Germain rallied late against Barcelona. Even in defeat, Lamine Yamal found space to decorate the room with a ludicrous toe-poke equaliser, and there was a wholesome tale in Italy as Scott McTominay scored twice for Napoli in their 4-3 win against Bodø/Glimt. These were his first strikes since returning from heart surgery, taking his tally at the club to 29 goals in 86 appearances. No wonder Erik ten Hag was peeved with his bosses at Manchester United for shipping the midfielder off to Naples. One has to admire the courage of Erik ten Hag, speaking out on Man United’s ‘toxic culture’ [yesterday’s Football Daily, full email edition]. I broke out in a cold sweat reading about how they ‘give power to the players’. The stuff of nightmares, really” – Rowan Sweeney. Roberto De Zerbi wants Spurs to be a family ( yesterday’s Football Daily )? And he thinks playing for or with a family will avoid relegation? Well, I have this uncle. He’s called Weird Uncle Fiver (now there’s a throwback – Football Daily Ed), and he loves to [snip – Football Daily lawyers, and time-travelling pedants]” – Mike Wilner. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: ‘A complete threat’: Rio Ngumoha’s electric display excites Van Dijk and Liverpool
item.description: Teenager produced man-of-the-match performance against Villarreal and has learned from Salah, says Reds captain The shot sailed wide of Peter Gulacsi’s top corner and into the Kop, affording Villarreal much-needed respite at 4-2, but for Andoni Iraola it was a standout moment in a scintillating Champions League display from Rio Ngumoha. To a coach that called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield. There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side ultimately won 4-3 , Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with the left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta has mastered the art of making substitutions at Arsenal
item.description: Arsenal have beaten Nottingham Forest, Sunderland and Leeds this season thanks to goals from players off the bench By Opta Analyst They say that once is an accident, twice is a coincidence and three times is a pattern. After Mikel Arteta’s substitutes proved decisive yet again for Arsenal, we can say with certainty that his ability to change games from his bench is a pattern worth noting. With Arsenal labouring away at Nottingham Forest and the game drifting towards a goalless draw, Noni Madueke – introduced at half-time – won the game for the visitors , shimmying inside and striking a heavily deflected right-footed shot past Matz Sels. It was hardly a glamorous goal but it secured three valuable Premier League points for Arteta’s side. Continue reading...

item.title: Foden hat-trick helps Manchester City cut through noise and crush AEK Athens
item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
item.description: As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry , a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26. Further to Peters and Lee [ Monday’s Football Daily letters] another 70s example that occurred to me was the West Ham players Mervyn Day and Bill Green . They were both in the West Ham United team from 1976-78, and in Carlisle United’s greatest season 1974-75. When Green was still at Carlisle, he played against West Ham’s Day. So plenty of Green Day commentary opportunities there. Of course, the band hadn’t formed yet, but who knows, perhaps they thought of the band’s name whilst watching some old 70s football footage” – Bob Dunning. On the subject of musical football matchups, all I can say is that it’s just a shame Gareth Barry was at Manchester City a few years too late to play alongside David White ” – Tim Russell. As an aside to the music makers and fitba’, in the late 60s at the old Highbury, we would be entertained at every first team match by the local constabulary brass band. Such was the style of play, it did introduce a some element of entertainment into our visits to the old stadium” – Tommy Boyd (and, surprisingly, others). This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Animal rights group urges Crystal Palace to retire bald eagle mascot

In a letter to Palace’s chief executive, Sharon Lacey, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) called on the club to end Phoenix’s appearances at Selhurst Park and commit never to use a live animal mascot again. item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Leaving England is scary but I’m here to win’: Charlie Cresswell on Ligue 1 life and his international dream
item.description: Young centre-back could not see a way forward at Leeds so moved to France. Now he’s preparing for the biggest game of his life against Juventus By Get French Football News “Leaving England is such a scary, scary decision,” says Charlie Cresswell. It is a decision that he never thought he would make. His father, Richard, made a career as a footballer in England; his brother, Alfie, was coming through Leeds’ academy; Charlie was on the fringes of their first team when the opportunity arose to join Toulouse in 2024. “That was the biggest decision I made in football,” he says. “I’ve been a Leeds fan since I was eight. I’d been at the club since I was 10, but, looking back, I was 20 years old with no games and I needed to get out and go play.” Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton John
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! There are only two things certain in life – death and taxes Reece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery was a cut-and-paste job from the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it contained an actual apology to Elton John and the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italian the same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house . Shall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy. Reading that ‘European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Infantino next year’ , I can’t be the only well informed reader to think that a certain intergalactic bin wearing member of the nobility would make a terrific candidate. Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid. Looking at the Benfica v Celtic game I was immediately drawn to the presence of two Durans. Have there been any other instances of any other bands being present in a game? Possibly in the Human League? I am hoping a Serie A game with a Scritti and a Politti … a French game with Depeche and Mode. You get the general idea” – Mike Turney. Continue reading...

item.title: My old teammate Miroslav Klose is bucking a trend in German coaching | Philipp Lahm
item.description: ‘Miro’, now in charge at Nürnberg, knows the value of consistency and identity in an era of tinkering coaches who did not play professionally You learn the most from the best. The Champions League winners are Paris Saint-Germain, and they could achieve a historic hat-trick this season. Since the tournament’s rebrand in 1992, they would be only the second club to accomplish this feat, after Real Madrid’s run from 2016 to 2018. I see clear parallels between the two. For Madrid, nine players started in all three of their final victories. Similarly, PSG won their two finals with virtually identical lineups. The only change came during their title defence in Budapest , where Gianluigi Donnarumma no longer featured in goal, Luis Enrique having parted ways with the Italian European champion. core players: about 70 to 85% each remaining regular starters: 50 to 60% each squad players: 40 to 45% each fringe squad places: sharing the remaining maximum of 20% Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City are suddenly box-office in age of charge-rage and mega defiance | Barney Ronay
item.description: This is by far the most interesting this club have ever been and they faced PSG, a kind of twin entity in all this as oil state glove puppets Another day, another note of unreality; another vivid and brilliant spectacle that feels as though it has been whipped together out of meringue and burnt sugar. Time flies when the world is closing in. Two weeks on, this was Manchester City’s first home game since the verdict dropped, the irrefutable body of evidence was refuted, and English football entered its state of ongoing whiplash. In the stadium this felt like watching someone dance while the world burns. This was a brilliant game pegged out around six goals , a collapse, a comeback, posts and bars struck, saved penalties, and a performance of state-of-the-art omni-football from this brilliantly high-grade Paris Saint-Germain team. Continue reading...

item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. Continue reading...

item.title: Have any footballers ended their career with more own goals than goals? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the earliest trophyless seasons, scoring off one’s backside (part II) and the origins of ‘shithousery’ Mail us with all of your questions and answers “How many professional players have ended their senior careers with more own goals than goals for their own team?” wonders Peter Clark. In the past we’ve looked at the players with the most own goals , but we haven’t looked at those who ended their professional career in debit. “Southampton cult hero Francis Benali scored only one ‘positive’ goal in his career and was legendary for banging in goal-of-the-month contenders at his own end, most notably a bullet header against Oldham in the 1993-94 season ,” writes Daz Pearce. We could only find a couple of OGs for Benali, the other being against Manchester United in 1999-2000 . But we were unable to find a comprehensive Southampton database, so there’s a chance we’ve missed some beauties. Continue reading...

item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: Sliding Doors meets Biff’s Almanac: City saga stirs up a world of alternate histories | Max Rushden
item.description: Even New Romantics have a view but this long story will not be cut short amid endless hypotheticals and split narratives It’s Wednesday afternoon (UK time) and I find myself interviewing Tony Hadley on TalkSport about his upcoming big band tour. We play a bit of Spandau Ballet, chat about the classics and his career – hanging out with Frank Sinatra and Tony Bennett. In as much as you can deduce in a 10-minute chat on Zoom, Tony seems like an absolute gent. We do always try to bring it back to sport – Tony is an Arsenal fan, there’s a bit of Arteta, Leeds at the weekend. Tony brings up Billy Bremner and suggests that my co-host Charlie Baker and I are too young to remember him playing. We are, and how wonderful to be called young. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...

item.title: Sign up for the Moving the Goalposts newsletter: our free women’s football email
item.description: Get our roundup of women’s football for free twice a week, featuring the insights of experts such as Ada Hegerberg and Magdalena Eriksson Join us as we delve deeper into the wonderful world of women’s football in our weekly newsletter. It is informative, entertaining, global, critical – when needed – and, above all, passionate. Written mainly by Júlia Belas Trindade and Sophie Downey , expect guest appearances from stars such as Anita Asante, Ada Hegerberg and many more. Try our other sports emails: as well as the occasionally funny football email The Fiver from Monday to Friday, there are weekly catch-ups for cricket in The Spin and rugby union in The Breakdown , and our seven-day roundup of the best of our sports journalism in The Recap .
